title: Foreshortening and projected limb length
plainLanguage: A limb pointing toward or away from the camera looks shorter even though the real limb has not shrunk. This is one of the main reasons a correct skeleton can look “wrong” in 2D.
purpose: Prevent the Corpus Pane from mistaking perspective changes for anatomy changes.

rules.statement: Projected length differences alone must not trigger an anatomy or schema change.
Tag strongly shortened regions as foreshortened and compare them preferentially with foreshortened references of compatible torso/head views.
If depth direction is unclear, record foreshortened with unknown depth direction rather than guessing toward/away.
A new artwork variant may be required even when the skeleton remains valid.

implementation.currentSupport: Corpus Pane records per-region projection state and optional depth-direction hints, and uses projection context during reference retrieval. Foreshortening remains a reviewed 2D observation, not a solved 3D pose.
implementation.futureWork: Expand the reviewed perspective-reference library and test whether projection-aware retrieval reduces correction work across more mannequin views.
